name: Computer Organisation
description: Instruction sets, datapath and control, pipelining, the memory hierarchy and I/O as they appear in GATE.

nodes.name: Instruction sets
nodes.desc: Machine instructions, registers, RISC versus CISC, and how an ISA describes a computer.
nodes.summary: You will be able to explain how an instruction set architecture describes a computer and compare RISC and CISC designs.

nodes.name: Instruction formats
nodes.desc: Fixed and expanding opcodes, operand fields and counting how many instructions fit an encoding.
nodes.summary: You will be able to design fixed and expanding opcode formats and count how many instructions fit an encoding.
topics: Zero, one, two and three address formats

nodes.name: Addressing modes
nodes.desc: Immediate, direct, indirect, register, indexed, relative and auto-increment addressing.
nodes.summary: You will be able to compute effective addresses for immediate, direct, indirect, register, indexed, relative and auto-increment modes.

nodes.name: Assembly programs
nodes.desc: Tracing short assembly programs: loops, the program counter, stack operations and flags.
nodes.summary: You will be able to trace short assembly programs through loops, program counter changes, stack operations and flags.

nodes.name: CPU performance
nodes.desc: CPI, clock rate, execution time, speedup and Amdahl's law.
nodes.summary: You will be able to compute CPU execution time from CPI and clock rate and apply speedup and Amdahl's law.

nodes.name: Datapath
nodes.desc: The ALU, register file and buses that execute instructions, and the steps of instruction execution.
nodes.summary: You will be able to describe how the ALU, register file and buses execute instructions and list the steps of instruction execution.

nodes.name: Register transfers
nodes.desc: Micro-operations on a single-bus datapath and counting the cycles an instruction takes.
nodes.summary: You will be able to write micro-operations for instructions on a single-bus datapath and count the cycles each takes.

nodes.name: Hardwired control
nodes.desc: Generating control signals with combinational and sequential logic.
nodes.summary: You will be able to explain how hardwired control units generate control signals with combinational and sequential logic.

nodes.name: Microprogramming
nodes.desc: Microprogrammed control: control memory, horizontal and vertical microinstructions, and control word sizes.
nodes.summary: You will be able to describe microprogrammed control and compute control word and control memory sizes for horizontal and vertical formats.

nodes.name: Pipelining
nodes.desc: Overlapping instruction execution in stages; pipeline registers and the ideal one-instruction-per-cycle.
nodes.summary: You will be able to explain how pipelining overlaps instruction execution in stages using pipeline registers to approach one instruction per cycle.

nodes.name: Pipeline speedup
nodes.desc: Speedup, throughput and latency with unequal stage delays and pipeline register overhead.
nodes.summary: You will be able to compute pipeline speedup, throughput and latency with unequal stage delays and register overhead.

nodes.name: Data hazards
nodes.desc: RAW, WAR and WAW dependences, stalls and operand forwarding.
nodes.summary: You will be able to identify RAW, WAR and WAW dependences, count stall cycles and apply operand forwarding.

nodes.name: Control hazards
nodes.desc: Branch penalties, delayed branches and their effect on the effective CPI.
nodes.summary: You will be able to compute branch penalties and effective CPI and explain delayed branches and branch prediction.

nodes.name: Memory hierarchy
nodes.desc: Locality and the levels of the hierarchy; average access time across levels.
nodes.summary: You will be able to explain locality and the memory hierarchy and compute average access time across levels.

nodes.name: Cache memory
nodes.desc: How a cache sits between CPU and memory, blocks, hits and misses.
nodes.summary: You will be able to explain how a cache sits between CPU and memory, organises data in blocks, and handles hits and misses.

nodes.name: Cache mapping
nodes.desc: Direct-mapped, set-associative and fully associative caches; splitting an address into tag, index and offset.
nodes.summary: You will be able to split an address into tag, index and offset for direct-mapped, set-associative and fully associative caches.

nodes.name: Cache performance
nodes.desc: Hit ratio, miss penalty, AMAT, multilevel caches and the kinds of misses.
nodes.summary: You will be able to compute hit ratio, miss penalty and AMAT for single and multilevel caches and classify cache misses.

nodes.name: Cache policies
nodes.desc: Replacement (LRU, FIFO) and write policies: write-through, write-back and write-allocate.
nodes.summary: You will be able to apply LRU and FIFO replacement and compare write-through, write-back and write-allocate policies.

nodes.name: Main memory
nodes.desc: Memory chips, address decoding, interleaving and banks; DRAM refresh and memory capacity.
nodes.summary: You will be able to design memory from chips with address decoding and analyse interleaving, banks and DRAM refresh.

nodes.name: Interrupts
nodes.desc: Interrupt-driven I/O, vectored interrupts, priorities and daisy chaining.
nodes.summary: You will be able to explain interrupt-driven I/O with vectored interrupts, priorities and daisy chaining.

nodes.name: Programmed I/O
nodes.desc: Polling, handshaking, memory-mapped versus isolated I/O and serial transfer rates.
nodes.summary: You will be able to compare polling, handshaking, memory-mapped and isolated I/O and compute serial transfer rates.

nodes.name: DMA
nodes.desc: Direct memory access, burst and cycle-stealing modes, and the CPU time DMA saves.
nodes.summary: You will be able to explain direct memory access in burst and cycle-stealing modes and compute the CPU time it saves.
